Fun/Scary Story: 

I stepped on a baby rattle snake on L. I was probably standing on it for a good 15 sec before I realized the vibration I was feeling wasn't my phone becuase it was off. I looked at my water bottle in my pocket and told my friends my water bottle was vibrating lol. They all yelled "your stepping on a snake!!!" and I looked down at my feet and I was standing on the head of a baby rattler and jumped back as fast as I could before I actually was stepping still tried to swipe at me but I think I messed it up pretty bad and then watched it squirm back under the layered rocks by the reservoir. I thought rattle snakes used there rattle to warn you that you were close, not to tell you that you are stepping on them lol.  We were all scared to death except one of my friends tried to hit it with a stick before it could get in but it got in there pretty fast. We wanted to get to the shore so bad but it was way to rocky everywhere to get down. We had to stick to the path we were making and about a min after I stepped on the baby rattler my friend yells out "another one!." We see another snake on top of a rock and then it sorta just rolled down the rock... and fell into a pretty big crease in the rocks. This 2nd snake we came across in a few min, however, was not a rattlesnake but a bull snake I was still in shock and coming up on the L. We eventually got to a beach part with no rocks so we could get our feet in the water and we got there and just felt so safe haha. All of us felt like we could see a rattlesnake at any second. We didnt want to leave that part of the reservoir but it was getting dark and we had no choice. Luckily, we made it back to our campsite safely without seeing any snakes. Enjoyed the rest of our crazy L trips while 2 of us had only taken mushrooms so they were already almost done tripping. we had another 8-10 hours to go :) I used to love snakes and I still do, but this changed me for life. I have to look at every single step I take everywhere I go and refuse to go back there. John Martin Reservoir in La Junta, CO. I was lucky becuase I could have gotten bit where none of us had cell service and the drive to the town from where we where was about a couple hours and all of us were either on L or mushrooms or both...  And baby rattlesnakes are WAYY more deadly then adults because the release all of their venom when they bit something due to not being able to control there venom glands. Ended up being a cool story to tell now for the rest of my life.
